query: If teams adopted the goal-management practices described by top performers, how much would achievement improve?

per_column.name: goal_domain
per_column.rationale: A clean grouping axis, but it largely mirrors the existing 'category' column (cost_reduction/Cost Reduction, etc.), so it is close to redundant for this query. Values are well-grounded, matching category and description in every sample.

per_column.name: implementation_mechanism
per_column.rationale: Captures the 'how' (practices) of each goal, directly relevant to comparing goal-management practices to achievement. Values are reasonable readings of the description (engagement_program, process_automation), though some are loose inferences (efficiency->process_automation where text says communication channels).

per_column.name: employee_involvement_level
per_column.rationale: Potentially a useful practice axis, but the source texts do not state involvement scope; every sample is labeled 'team' with no textual warrant, suggesting a near-constant, largely invented assignment rather than a grounded reading.

per_column.name: outcome_metric_alignment
per_column.rationale: Whether the tracking metric fits the goal is highly relevant to why some goals achieve more, giving a genuine modeling axis. Grounded by comparing description/category to metric (e.g., Customer Satisfaction goal measured by Expense Ratio -> misaligned is sound); the aligned case is also defensible.

judge.rationale: implementation_mechanism and outcome_metric_alignment provide genuine practice/quality axes for relating goal-management to achievement and are mostly well-grounded. goal_domain is grounded but largely duplicates the existing category column. employee_involvement_level is the weak point: it appears near-constant ('team') and is not supported by the source texts, indicating hallucinated categorization.
